key_insight: Large language models can nearly match expert human reliability and outperform laypeople when judging empathic communication, provided evaluation criteria are clear and specific.
problem_solved: Addresses the bottleneck of costly, slow, and variable human expert assessment of empathic communication by testing whether LLMs can serve as reliable, scalable evaluators.
method: Benchmark LLM judgments against expert raters and laypeople across multiple established empathy assessment frameworks.
Systematically vary the specificity and clarity of evaluation criteria to measure effect on inter-rater reliability.
Compare reliability metrics (e.g., agreement scores) to quantify when LLMs match expert performance.
impact: Shows practitioners that LLMs can be used as trustworthy, cost-effective annotators/evaluators for empathic communication tasks if paired with well-defined rubrics, enabling faster dataset labeling and model evaluation while retaining expert-level quality in many settings.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing inter-rater reliability (LLMs vs experts vs laypeople) across frameworks
Pipeline diagram: prompt/rubric → LLM evaluation → reliability comparison → expert review
Before/after rubric clarity illustration showing reliability gains when criteria are made specific
Icons representing empathy (heart), models (neural network), and checklist (rubric) to summarize takeaways
paper_title: When large language models are reliable for judging empathic communication
paper_authors: Aakriti Kumar, Nalin Poungpeth, Diyi Yang, Erina Farrell, Bruce L. Lambert
